title: Where Does Electricity Come From? Gizmo Finds Out
intro: Hi, friends! I'm Gizmo the robot, and welcome to Gizmo Explains!
I love asking, how does that work? Today we're going to find out where energy comes from.
We'll explore five cool things. Can you count them with me? One, two, three, four, five!
When my antenna lights up, it means I have an idea!

lines: Here's a clue: it goes inside toys and flashlights! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
A battery stores energy inside it, ready to use.
When it's connected, it sends electricity through wires to make toys move and lights shine!
Can you light up like a flashlight? Click! Shine!
One more time, nice and loud: BATTERY!
Only grown-ups should change batteries. We keep them away from our mouths.
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: it's a flat, shiny panel that loves the sun! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
A solar panel catches sunlight with special flat squares.
It turns that sunlight into electricity, which can power lights in a home!
Can you open your arms wide, like a panel catching sunshine?
What does a solar panel need?
Let's say it together: SOLAR PANEL!
One more time, nice and loud: SOLAR PANEL!
Some calculators and garden lights have tiny solar panels on them.
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: it's very tall, with three long blades! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
Wind pushes on the long blades and makes them spin.
Inside, the spinning makes electricity that travels through wires to homes and schools!
Can you spin your arms slowly, like turbine blades in the wind?
What makes a wind turbine spin?
Let's say it together: WIND TURBINE!
One more time, nice and loud: WIND TURBINE!
Lots of wind turbines together are called a wind farm.
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: it's a big wheel that turns in a river! Can you guess?
Now let's look at: Water Wheel!
How does it work? Let's find out!
Flowing water pushes on the paddles around the wheel.
The push makes the wheel spin, and the spinning can do work, like grinding grain into flour!
Can you make your hands go round and round, like a water wheel?
Let's say it together: WATER WHEEL!
One more time, nice and loud: WATER WHEEL!
Today, big dams use moving water to make electricity too.
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: it's on the wall, and it goes click! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
Electricity needs a full loop of wire, like a circle, to flow.
Click on, and the loop is joined, so the light shines. Click off, and there's a gap, so the light goes out!
Can you click a pretend switch? On! Off! On!
It makes a gap, so electricity stops!
Let's say it together: LIGHT SWITCH!
One more time, nice and loud: LIGHT SWITCH!
Ask a grown-up to help with switches, and never touch plugs or outlets.
Now we know how it works. Great job!

recap: Wow, we learned so much! Let's remember.
And switches open and close the loop!
outro: Which one was your favorite? Keep asking, how does that work?
Bye, friends! See you next time on Gizmo Explains!
